name: DEEP STRATA: Lives Unlived
description: Deep Strata sells what it calls 'temporal lives' — complete neural simulations of historically reconstructed existences ranging from a 1920s Shanghai textile worker to a 2090 Lagos climate engineer, each lasting between 72 and 200 subjective hours of lived experience compressed into real-time sessions of 6-12 hours. The BCI feed is so complete that players emerge with genuine episodic memories, emotional attachments, and occasionally, language fragments from the simulated period. Psychiatrists in GLMZ are divided on whether these implanted memory-lives constitute a therapeutic tool or a dissociation vector.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 accountant emerges from a Deep Strata session convinced she has unfinished business from her simulated life — and begins acting on memories that aren't real.
Someone has been smuggling unauthorized life-packages into the Deep Strata library: simulations of people who are still alive, their neural patterns harvested without consent.
A Deep Strata archivist discovers a life-package dated 2231 — five years in the future — and it depicts GLMZ in ruins.
